title: Burj Khalifa
blurb: The world’s tallest building: an 828 m Y-shaped tower in Dubai designed by Adrian Smith of SOM and opened in 2010. Three buttressed wings step back in 27 spiral setbacks around a central core, rising from a piled raft through a hotel, residences and offices to a 242.5 m steel spire.

sourceUrls.label: SOM: Design and Construction of the Burj Khalifa (PDF)
Geotechnical case study: Burj Khalifa piled raft (PDF)

systems.name: Foundations
systems.description: The 3.7 m reinforced-concrete piled raft and its 192 bored piles, spreading the tower’s weight over the desert ground.

systems.name: Podium and entrances
systems.description: The podium block at the tower’s base with its entrances, hotel lobby, office annex, forecourt and two parking levels.

systems.name: Central core
systems.description: The hexagonal buttressed core that carries the tower’s height and houses its vertical transportation.

systems.name: Wings
systems.description: The three Y-shaped wings in 27 stepped tiers, spiralling back as the tower rises.

systems.name: Setback terraces
systems.description: The outdoor terraces and parapets left behind at each setback, with schematic tip caps on the wing ends.

systems.name: Cladding
systems.description: The glass curtain wall: 142,000 m2 of panels with vertical tubular fins and spandrel bands.

systems.name: Spire and crown
systems.description: The steel crown above the concrete and the 242.5 m spire with its 200 m pinnacle pipe.

systems.name: Mechanical systems
systems.description: Mechanical floors, refuge floors, the chilled-water plant and water storage tanks.

systems.name: Elevators and stairs
systems.description: The 57 elevators and 8 escalators: core shafts, double-deck observation cars, service cars and wing egress stairs.

systems.name: Lake and fountains
systems.description: The 12-hectare Burj Khalifa Lake, the Dubai Fountain, the boardwalk and the park.

systems.name: Interiors
systems.description: The vertical city inside: hotel, residences, offices, sky lobbies, restaurants and observation decks.

explanations.piled raft foundation: The reinforced-concrete raft under the tower, 3.7 m thick, poured in four separate sections (three wings and the centre core). Its three wings are each about 50 m long and 25 m wide. Wing outlines are schematic.
explanations.bored piles: 192 bored cast-in-place piles, 1.5 m in diameter and about 47 m deep, carrying the raft in the weak desert ground. (One geotechnical paper counts 194.) Pile layout is schematic.
explanations.podium: The low podium block wrapping the tower’s base, holding lobbies, retail and back-of-house space. The real podium includes a 4 to 6 storey garage and an office annex; massing here is schematic.
explanations.podium curtain wall: Glass walls wrapping the podium block. Subdivision is schematic.
explanations.main entrance: One of the tower’s entrances at the podium level. Position and canopy shape are schematic.
explanations.hotel entrance: The Armani Hotel’s entrance at the podium level. Position and canopy shape are schematic.
explanations.residential entrance: The residences’ entrance at the podium level. Position and canopy shape are schematic.
explanations.armani hotel lobby: The Armani Hotel lobby at concourse level, part of the 304-room hotel occupying 15 of the lower 39 floors. Interior layout is schematic.
explanations.office annex: The office annex building beside the tower, for which NORR designed a 6-storey addition. Massing is schematic.
explanations.parking level b1: The first of two subterranean parking levels. Layout is schematic.
explanations.parking level b2: The second subterranean parking level. Layout is schematic.
explanations.arrival forecourt: The arrival forecourt in front of the podium. Extent is schematic.
explanations.central core, lower: The lower section of the hexagonal buttressed core, the structural spine that carries the tower’s height. The Y-shaped tripartite plan of three wings on a central core is sourced; core radii are schematic.
explanations.central core, middle: The middle section of the hexagonal buttressed core, narrowing as the wings step back around it. Radii are schematic.
explanations.central core, upper: The upper section of the hexagonal buttressed core above the last wing setbacks. Radii are schematic.
explanations.central core, crown: The crown of the concrete core, rising to the 585.4 m top-floor level where the steelwork takes over. The structure is all reinforced concrete to level 156. Radii are schematic.
explanations.spire base steelwork: The steel braced frame from level 156 (585.4 m) upward, where the concrete structure ends. Above the pinnacle base the spire is 242.5 m of structural steel weighing more than 4,000 tonnes. Taper is schematic.
explanations.spire cross bracing: Diagonal steel bracing on the spire base, part of the braced-frame system above level 156. Bracing layout is schematic.
explanations.pinnacle pipe: The central pinnacle pipe: 200 m tall, weighing 350 tonnes, rising to the 828 m tip. It also houses communications equipment. Diameter is schematic.
explanations.pinnacle collar rings: Collar rings stiffening the pinnacle pipe along its 200 m rise. Positions are schematic.
explanations.crown roof: The roof slab at 739.4 m, the highest solid roof of the steel crown. Shape is schematic.
explanations.crown terraces: Terraces on the crown where the concrete core gives way to the steel spire. Shape is schematic.
explanations.aviation beacon: The red aviation warning beacon at the 828 m tip. Position is schematic.
explanations.communications equipment: Communications equipment housed in the spire, part of the pinnacle structure. Placement is schematic.
explanations.lower mechanical plant: Mechanical plant in the basement levels serving the tower’s systems. Layout is schematic.
explanations.mechanical level, low: A mechanical floor band in the lower tower. Exact level is schematic.
explanations.mechanical level, mid: A mechanical floor band in the mid tower. Exact level is schematic.
explanations.mechanical level, high: A mechanical floor band in the upper tower. Exact level is schematic.
explanations.refuge floors: Refuge floors where occupants can gather in an emergency, spaced through the tower. Levels are schematic.
explanations.chilled water plant: The chilled-water plant for the air-conditioning system, which at peak cooling matches about 13,000 short tons of melting ice per day. Layout is schematic.
explanations.water storage tanks: Water storage tanks: the tower’s water system supplies an average of 946,000 litres per day through 100 km of pipes. Tank positions are schematic.
explanations.core elevator shafts: Elevator shafts in the central core, which houses all vertical transportation. The tower has 57 elevators and 8 escalators. Shaft count and routing are schematic.
explanations.double-deck observation elevators: The double-deck observation elevators rising to the 124th floor deck, the world’s fastest double-deckers at up to 10 m/s. Routing is schematic.
explanations.service elevators: Service elevators running the full height of the occupied tower. Routing is schematic.
explanations.elevator machine rooms: Elevator machine rooms at the top of the concrete core, driving the 57 elevators including the 504 m longest-travel cars. Layout is schematic.
explanations.escalators: Escalators in the podium and concourse levels, part of the 8 escalators in the complex. Positions are schematic.
explanations.burj khalifa lake: The 12-hectare (30-acre) artificial Burj Khalifa Lake at the tower’s base. Outline and position are schematic.
explanations.dubai fountain jets: The Dubai Fountain’s main jets on the lake: the 275 m choreographed fountain by WET Design shoots water to 152.4 m. Jet layout is schematic.
explanations.fountain nozzle field: The field of fountain nozzles, lit by 6,600 lights and 25 coloured projectors. Grid is schematic.
explanations.lake boardwalk: The boardwalk along the lake edge for watching the fountain shows. Position is schematic.
explanations.burj park: Parkland around the tower, part of the Downtown Dubai landscaping. Shape is schematic.
explanations.armani hotel: The 304-room Armani Hotel, the first of four by Armani, occupying 15 of the lower 39 floors (opened 27 April 2010). Interior zoning is schematic.
explanations.hotel spa and pool: Spa and pool facilities within the Armani Hotel zone. Layout is schematic.
explanations.residential lobby: The residential lobby, whose display includes the work of Jaume Plensa among more than 1,000 art pieces in the tower. Layout is schematic.
explanations.residential apartments: 900 private residential apartments on floors 20 through 108, which the developer says sold out within eight hours. Interior zoning is schematic.
explanations.corporate suites: Corporate suites on the upper office floors. Interior zoning is schematic.
explanations.corporate offices: Corporate offices filling most of the remaining floors above the residences. Interior zoning is schematic.
explanations.sky lobby, level 43: The sky lobby on the 43rd floor, one of two sky lobbies housing swimming pools. Height is approximate; interior is schematic.
explanations.sky lobby, level 76: The sky lobby on the 76th floor with a swimming pool, plus the outdoor zero-entry pool on the same floor. Height is approximate; interior is schematic.
explanations.at.mosphere restaurant: At.mosphere on the 122nd floor at 442 m, the world’s highest restaurant. Interior is schematic.
explanations.level 123 sky lobby: The sky lobby on the 123rd floor, just above At.mosphere. Interior is schematic.
explanations.observation deck, level 124: The At the Top observation deck on the 124th floor at 452 m, with indoor and outdoor terraces (opened 5 January 2010). Interior is schematic.
explanations.observation deck, level 125: The upper level of the At the Top observation deck on the 125th floor. Height is schematic; interior is schematic.
explanations.at the top sky, level 148: At the Top SKY on the 148th floor at 555 m, which held the world’s highest observation deck record when it opened on 15 October 2014. Interior is schematic.
explanations.the lounge observatory: The Lounge observatory at 585 m, the world’s highest lounge (opened February 2019), at the top occupied level. Interior is schematic.
explanations.curtain wall, central core: The glass curtain wall wrapping the central core. The full cladding system is 142,000 m2 of panels; subdivision here is schematic.
explanations.crown cladding: Cladding on the steel crown above the concrete core. Subdivision is schematic.
